risks.finding: A link whose destination holds a character reference or a backslash escape keeps main's undecoded href in a live tree that main's server wrote. The first write by this build re-escapes that href, so the stored markdown, the version view and a comment then open another address (version 2 stored '[amp](https://x.test/?a=1&amp;b=2)'; main's comment of the same markdown linked 'https://x.test/?a=1&b=2').
risks.evidence: Real surface: a throwaway Playwright probe wrote the spec through main's server (pmdoc at 690c0136), then edited it through the head's server against the same database. The head's v2 and v3 held '&amp;', '&copy;', '\\&amp;' and 'a\\\\' in the four links. Census of every stored version in production (13 projects, 6,474 documents, 31,576 distinct versions): 0 versions hold such a link outside code, and 0 versions have a link the head reads differently from main's tree. A docs-package regression test (TestAnEditKeepsTheLinkALiveTreeFromTheBuildBeforeHeld, saved at $TMPDIR/infra531-test/main-era-tree-red-test.patch) fails at the head. It was not committed, because a pass needs a migration of live trees and that migration would touch no stored document today.
risks.decisionFor: architect: accept with the census re-run after the deploy, or order a live-tree migration
